What Media Says

Voices from global media on KBW2026

Voices from global media on KBW2026

What Media Say

What Media SayS

What Media SayS

  • WSJ

    "...Access for corporate customers (in South Korea) would expand in stages as regulations permit, with the company building custody capabilities, infrastructure and internal controls to support broader participation."

  • The Block

    "Crypto never needed conventional market hours because the asset class is inherently international, and that traditional exchanges have begun extending sessions. Instead, onchain's lasting advantages come from allowing users to keep custody of their own funds, which helps prevent a common point of failure. Onchain finance really, at its core, means that users have still retained control and custody of their funds. I think that's the number one thing," - Hyperliquid Co-founder Jeff Yan

  • The Dong-A Ilbo

    "At this year's KBW2026, a clear shift emerged in how people view digital assets. No longer just something to buy and sell as an investment, digital assets are now being discussed as financial infrastructure spanning payments, settlement and custody."

  • CoinMarketCap

    "Prior bull markets were driven mainly by initial coin offerings, non-fungible tokens, meme coins, and stablecoins. He expects this cycle to be shaped instead by tokenization, artificial intelligence, and improved regulatory conditions for digital assets." - Bitmine Immersion Technologies Chairman Tom Lee

  • Incrypted

    "South Korea became East Asia's largest crypto market from July 2025 to June 2026, building an economy worth $449.1 billion. Its crypto market grew 12.3% year over year, with retail investors remaining the main driver as they actively traded tokens tied to artificial intelligence (AI)...One of the Korean market's defining features was the popularity of AI tokens. By June 2026, they had become the largest thematic category by share of trading volume in Korean won, surpassing, among others, payment tokens such as XRP. Trading volumes in AI cryptocurrencies against the Korean won were 19.5 times higher than the same metric for the Japanese yen."
